metadata.rainfall_source: forecast (JMA GSM via Open-Meteo Previous Runs API, issued on the as-of date)

forecast.rainfall_source: forecast (JMA GSM via Open-Meteo Previous Runs API, issued on the as-of date)
forecast.flood_signal: Sum of three local (Asia/Karachi) days: day D from the stitched short-lead series (`precipitation`), day D+1 from the run issued ~1 day earlier (`precipitation_previous_day1`), day D+2 from the run issued ~2 days earlier (`precipitation_previous_day2`). All three come from model runs initialised on or around day D, i.e. what a 3-day forecast issued on D said.
forecast.drought_signal: Both runs: sum of observed daily precipitation_sum from the Historical Weather API over D-30..D and D-90..D inclusive, mirroring production's archive call with past_days=30/90 (which returns today plus the previous N days). Missing days are skipped, as in production.

hindsight.flood_signal: Observed daily precipitation_sum (Open-Meteo Historical Weather API, default model, ECMWF IFS analysis at 9 km for these years) for days D, D+1 and D+2, treated as a perfect 3-day forecast. This uses data from after the as-of date and is an upper bound on what the scorer could achieve, not a predictive test.
hindsight.drought_signal: Both runs: sum of observed daily precipitation_sum from the Historical Weather API over D-30..D and D-90..D inclusive, mirroring production's archive call with past_days=30/90 (which returns today plus the previous N days). Missing days are skipped, as in production.

metadata.forecast_model_note: Production calls api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast with the default best_match model. That blend's lead-time archive does not cover 2021-2022 (Previous Runs API returns nulls), so the forecast run uses JMA GSM (~55 km), the only model found with lead-time data for both years. Expect it to be coarser than production.

scorer.note: Production tries Gemini first and only uses this rule-based scorer as a fallback. This backtest evaluates the rule-based path only; Gemini was not called.

thresholds.flood: high if 3-day rainfall > 100 mm, medium if > 40 mm, else low; low if rainfall missing
thresholds.drought: always low (30/90-day rainfall is reported in the reason text but not used for the level)

leakage_checks.conclusion: HAZARD_CONTEXT only feeds the reason text of the rule-based scorer; replacing it with empty entries changes no risk level, so nothing in it can leak 2022 outcomes into this backtest. It would reach Gemini's prompt, which is not exercised here.
leakage_checks.district_selection_caveat: The 16 districts and their hazard labels were chosen in 2026 from NDMA material that postdates 2022, and the flood list overlaps the 2022 footprint. That choice cannot be undone here, so this backtest measures timing and the 2022-vs-2021 contrast, not whether the product picks the right districts.

evaluation_notes: impact_reference_date is a documented-by upper bound; true onset may be earlier.

first_high_2022 is the first as-of date flagged high anywhere in the window. For several districts it falls on an earlier rain spell (early July), so days_first_high_before_reference is not a lead time for the documented impact.

outcome looks only at as-of dates from reference-10 days to the reference date. The 10-day window was chosen after viewing the timelines; the full per-date series is included so other windows can be checked.
Districts whose hazard is not flood get a constant level from the scorer, so they carry no timing or year-contrast signal.

ground_truth.observed_hazard: monsoon rain flooding, then prolonged riverine/hill-torrent inundation
ground_truth.notes: Among the nine districts in Sindh's first calamity-hit notification (Fri 12 Aug 2022, during the fourth monsoon spell); also in the 23-district notification of Sun 21 Aug. District-specific onset date not pinned down; earlier July impacts in Sindh are reported only at province level. OCHA (4 Oct) expected Dadu to stay partially inundated until year end.

ground_truth.observed_hazard: flash flooding (the opposite of the drought hazard Risk Flag assigns)
ground_truth.notes: Dawn (30 Jul) reports overnight rain on 29 Jul causing flash floods in Chagai and Naushki: ~30 breaches on the Dalbandin rail section and ~20 on Nokkundi-Taftan (both in Chagai), and ~100 houses washed away across the two districts; the Pakistan-Iran train stayed suspended for ~25 days. OCHA SitRep 3 (26 Aug) lists UN food assistance to 4,350 households in Chagai within the flood response; SitRep 4 lists hygiene kits in Chaghi. Balochistan declared 32 of 34 districts calamity-hit on 31 Aug, but no source found naming the two excluded districts, so Chagai's status is unconfirmed.

ground_truth.observed_hazard: rain flooding (the opposite of the drought hazard Risk Flag assigns)
ground_truth.notes: Explicitly excluded from the 21 Aug Sindh notification (all of Sindh except Karachi and Tharparkar). OCHA (4 Oct), citing UNOSAT, reports floodwaters still increasing in Tharparkar during 15-21 Sep; the reference date is the end of that week, outside the backtest window. OCHA's 13 Sep snapshot map is NOT evidence of a declaration: it labels every Sindh district, including Karachi South/West and Malir, which were not notified. Later status unknown (PDMA Sindh says emergency was declared in 24 of 30 districts; the 24th was not identified).

summary.false_alarm_note: Every flood district in scope was affected in 2022, so false alarms cannot be measured from 2022 alone. High flags in 2021 are reported as candidate false alarms, but 2021 impacts were not researched, so they are unverified.
